findings.failure_path: The child can execute started.set() and then be descheduled before record_local_review(). After one second, the parent observes it alive, writes 40 and releases the lock. When the child resumes, either mutant can read 40, write 41 with the rewritten timestamp, and exit 0. Every assertion passes despite the missing or misplaced lock.
findings.smallest_fix: Emit the synchronization event from a child-local wrapper around the controller's actual LOCK_EX call, preserving the real flock, and require that event before rewriting. A removed lock then misses the event, while a read-before-lock necessarily precedes the rewrite. Verify this with a forced delay after process startup.

findings.failure_path: An I/O error during the receipt rewrite bypasses unlock, close, kill, and reap. The non-daemon writer remains blocked on the held lock, and multiprocessing shutdown can join it indefinitely instead of reporting the original test failure.
findings.smallest_fix: Put lock release and child cleanup in a finally block covering all operations after acquisition/start, so errors release the lock and stop/reap the writer before propagating.

findings.failure_path: After the bounded join expires, writer.join() waits without a timeout. SIGKILL does not guarantee prompt reaping when a process is stuck in uninterruptible I/O, so this path can still hang the suite and directly violates the bounded-wait acceptance.
findings.smallest_fix: Bound the post-kill reap and provide a bounded failure path for an unreaped child, including avoiding an implicit unbounded multiprocessing shutdown join.
